meta.title: How Careem Became Pakistan's $3 Billion Startup
titleOptions: The Pakistani Startup That Sold for $3 Billion
How One Startup Built 100+ Pakistani Companies
The Deal That Started Pakistan's Startup Boom
meta.topic: How Careem sparked Pakistan's startup generation
meta.description: How a ride-hailing startup co-founded by a Pakistani became a $3 billion exit — and launched a whole generation of founders. The Careem story. (Urdu-English narration, English captions.)

lines.text: پاکستان کی سب سے بڑی startup wave کیسے شروع ہوئی؟
lines.caption: How did Pakistan's biggest startup wave begin?

lines.text: دو ہزار بارہ میں ایک ride-hailing startup بنی: Careem۔
lines.caption: In 2012, a ride-hailing startup was born: Careem.

lines.text: اس کے co-founder مدثر شیخا ایک Pakistani تھے۔
lines.caption: Co-founder Mudassir Sheikha is Pakistani.
lines.name: Mudassir Sheikha

lines.text: Careem نے Pakistan اور Middle East میں تیزی سے grow کیا۔
lines.caption: Careem spread fast across Pakistan and the Middle East.

lines.text: پھر دو ہزار بیس میں Uber نے Careem کو acquire کر لیا۔
lines.caption: Then in 2020, Uber acquired Careem.

lines.text: لیکن اصل کہانی اس deal کے بعد شروع ہوتی ہے۔
lines.caption: But the real story starts after the sale.

lines.text: Careem کے سابق employees نے ایک نئی startup wave شروع کی۔
lines.caption: Former Careem staff launched a wave of new startups.

lines.text: سو سے زیادہ نئی companies Careem کے لوگوں نے بنائیں۔
lines.caption: companies founded by Careem alumni

lines.text: Pakistan میں اسے Careem Mafia کہا جاتا ہے۔
lines.caption: In Pakistan, they call it the 'Careem Mafia'.

lines.text: انہوں نے fintech، delivery اور B2B companies بنائیں۔
lines.caption: What the Careem Mafia built

lines.text: ایک company ختم ہو سکتی ہے، مگر impact باقی رہتا ہے۔
lines.caption: A company can end — but its impact remains.
